title: Ultrahuman announces Heart Scan feature for Ring Air and Ring Pro users
description: Ultrahuman's Ring Air gained atrial fibrillation (AFib) detection support in July 2024, and the Ring Pro, which launched in February this year, had it from the start. Today, Ultrahuman announced the Heart Scan feature, which builds on the AFib PowerPlug. Heart Scan is powered by FibriCheck and lets eligible Ring Air and Ring Pro users run an on-demand heart rhythm check when they want, unlike the AFib screening that runs nightly in the background. title: Amazon UK Prime Deals: Get near-flagship performance with the Poco F9 Pro at one-third off
description: The Poco F9 Pro offers near-flagship performance at under £600. It is powered by the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 V series chipset – the CPU is the same as on the flagship 8 Elite Gen 5 chip (with 2x 4.61GHz and 6x 3.63GHz Oryon cores), but the GPU has two-thirds the compute units. The V series compares favorably against the Snapdragon 8 Gen 5 (non-Elite) as it has higher CPU clock speeds and 12MB of Adreno High Performance Memory (HPM). title: Spotify is expanding Audiobooks to more than 180 markets
description: Audiobooks on Spotify are currently accessible in 22 markets. Today, Spotify announced that it will expand audiobooks to more than 180 markets by the end of 2026. This expansion would allow Spotify's 750 million users worldwide to stream or purchase books on Spotify. Listeners in new markets would gain access to over 350,000 titles in more than 120 languages, including new catalogs in Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, and Polish. title: Apple needs to pay an extra $184 million in Apple Watch patent infringement case
description: Apple received some bad news today. The company has been ordered to pay an additional $184 million in interest on top of a jury's previous $634 million verdict in a patent infringement case with Masimo. The initial verdict came out in November of last year, when a jury found that Apple infringed upon Masimo's patents related to the use of heart-rate monitoring features in its Apple Watches. Masimo was then awarded $634 million in damages. Now, judge James Selna rejected Apple’s argument that adding interest would constitute a windfall for Masimo, citing US Supreme Court guidance...
